title: Toast in the Kitchen  (厨房里的举杯)

segments.t: 泰莎、凯勒布和欧文在面向阳光庭院的厨房门口，听着伊芙琳的华尔兹飘过石板地，他们碰响茶杯庆祝检查通过。先完整听一遍吧。
Hear how effortlessly the second half flows from the first, Caleb?
You cannot even tell where thirty years ago ends and today begins.
And not one squeak on middle D. Graham earned two slices of lemon tart!
Raise your teacups, boys: to Room Nine and our saved courtyard!
To Chef Tessa, who ran an entire cafe kitchen from two pillows!
By Friday evening your ankle will be ready to greet every regular on the street.
Wait, look past the courtyard tree toward the open street gate, Caleb.
An older gentleman with a gray hat stopped right outside on the sidewalk.
He took his hat off when the piano reached the second page...
Wait a second: he is humming the exact melody along with Evelyn!
How could a stranger on the street know an unpublished waltz from a locked room?!
Call Hannah to the gate right now. Do not let him walk away!
现在，让我们仔细听听厨房门口这段交谈。
Hear how effortlessly the second half flows from the first, Caleb?
「听这下半段接上半段接得多自然啊，凯勒布？」 这个词由表示“努力”的 effort 加上表示“没有”的后缀 -less 组成，
how effortlessly
用来赞美一段听起来毫不费力、浑然天成的音乐衔接。
You cannot even tell where thirty years ago ends and today begins.
「你甚至都听不出三十年前的部分在哪里结束，今天的部分在哪里开始。」 和 can 或 cannot 连用时，动词 tell 在这里变成了“分辨”或“看出区别”的意思，
You cannot even tell
也就是“根本分辨不出断点”。
And not one squeak on middle D. Graham earned two slices of lemon tart!
「中央 D 键一下都没吱吱响。格雷厄姆赢得两块柠檬挞！」 老旧弹簧或干燥部件发出的尖锐声音叫做
not one squeak
证明了格雷厄姆换的新毛毡让琴键完美无瑕。
Raise your teacups, boys: to Room Nine and our saved courtyard!
「举起你们的茶杯，小伙子们：为九号房间和我们保住的庭院干杯！」 提议敬酒时，用及物动词
Raise your teacups
举起杯子，后面再跟上介词 to 来引出敬酒的对象或理由。
To Chef Tessa, who ran an entire cafe kitchen from two pillows!
「敬泰莎主厨，她靠两个枕头就指挥了整个咖啡馆厨房！」 动词 run 的不规则过去式，在这里的意思是“管理”或“掌管”：
ran an entire cafe kitchen
她甚至都没离开过椅子！
By Friday evening your ankle will be ready to greet every regular on the street.
「到了周五晚上，你的脚踝就能准备好在街上迎接每一位常客了。」 在咖啡馆和街区小店里，这个词作为可数名词，
every regular
指的是那些每周都会光顾的忠实老邻居。
Wait, look past the courtyard tree toward the open street gate, Caleb.
「等等，视线越过庭院的树，往敞开的临街大门那边看，凯勒布。」 作为表示动作或视线方向的介词，
look past
引导视线越过近处的参照物看向更远的地方。
An older gentleman with a gray hat stopped right outside on the sidewalk.
「一位戴着灰帽子的老绅士正好停在外面的人行道上。」 这个比较级比直接说 old 要礼貌和亲切得多，
An older gentleman
完全等同于我们说的“一位老先生”。
He took his hat off when the piano reached the second page...
「当钢琴弹到第二页时，他摘下了帽子……」 这个可分短语动词 take off 在这里把宾语夹在了中间，
took his hat off
这是一个表达敬意和感动的经典动作。
Wait a second: he is humming the exact melody along with Evelyn!
「等一下：他正在跟着伊芙琳准确地哼着这首旋律！」 闭着嘴巴哼唱一段旋律，在英语里叫作
he is humming
而 along with 表示他正分毫不差地跟着钢琴的节奏一起哼。
How could a stranger on the street know an unpublished waltz from a locked room?!
「街上的陌生人怎么会知道一首被锁在房间里的未发表的华尔兹？！」 否定前缀 un- 加在过去分词 published 前面，直接构成了
an unpublished waltz
形容一部从未印刷或出版过的作品。
Call Hannah to the gate right now. Do not let him walk away!
「马上叫汉娜去门口。别让他走开！」 沿着街道走远的动作可以用这个短语动词来表达，
walk away
其中的 away 强调了“离开、走远”的意思。让我们从厨房门口再听一遍这个场景吧。
Hear how effortlessly the second half flows from the first, Caleb?
You cannot even tell where thirty years ago ends and today begins.
And not one squeak on middle D. Graham earned two slices of lemon tart!
Raise your teacups, boys: to Room Nine and our saved courtyard!
To Chef Tessa, who ran an entire cafe kitchen from two pillows!
By Friday evening your ankle will be ready to greet every regular on the street.
Wait, look past the courtyard tree toward the open street gate, Caleb.
An older gentleman with a gray hat stopped right outside on the sidewalk.
He took his hat off when the piano reached the second page...
Wait a second: he is humming the exact melody along with Evelyn!
How could a stranger on the street know an unpublished waltz from a locked room?!
Call Hannah to the gate right now. Do not let him walk away!
敞开的大门外，一个路人居然对这首被锁在书柜里三十年的曲子的每一个音符都了如指掌！第五集的最后一个场景——让我们来听听。
See you soon!
